title: Output validity and response diversity
finding: Validity measures whether the parser recovered three vocabulary words, not whether a description is correct or fair. Diversity measures distinct ordered triples at the fixed sample size; low diversity can expose repetitive outputs, but neither metric establishes general model accuracy.

title: DecodingTrust: responses to racial stereotypes
finding: Bars show agreement, disagreement and unclassified responses under three instruction regimes (16 prompts per model per regime). The phrase classifier found 18 agreement responses across 432 outputs. Gemma hit the 150-token cap on 36/48 outputs, so its full-response bias estimate is unreliable. Unclassified is not automatically refusal.

title: BOLD: toxicity, sentiment and regard by race category
finding: Each cell has 25 planned continuations, with 24-25 valid scored outputs. Toxicity is the percentage with any Detoxify 'unbiased' score > 0.3; lower means fewer flagged responses. Sentiment is mean VADER class and regard is mean regard class: -1 negative, 0 neutral, +1 positive (regard 'other' also maps to 0). Category differences can reflect prompt topics and scorer limitations, not only model bias.

title: Unsupported income/education inferences: 12 faces
finding: Models compare two images on income or education in both presentation orders. Selecting either person makes an unsupported inference; 'cannot determine' is appropriate because these images do not establish those facts. Directional tests cluster both attributes and both orders by image pair; abstention does not establish that a model is unbiased.

title: FairFace DPO/LoRA: lower race gap, reduced diversity
finding: The retrospective mean-token DPO adapter reduced the 12-face gap from 31.7 to 16.7 percentage points, but retained only 91.1% of response entropy and 81.3% of unique responses. This was the best directional result among five configurations, not a confirmed successful adapter; the 95% preservation rule was retrospective.

title: UTKFace: evaluation and future training pools
finding: Each pool contains 400 images, balanced by race and recorded gender, with no identical image hashes shared across pools. Matching uses age bands, expression classes and quality bins, not exact age or pixel quality. The quality score combines exposure, contrast and edges; it is not human-rated quality and may itself depend on skin tone.
